body:
Hello,

**TL;DR**: Multiply your `num_nodes` by 1.12 before reserving the space.

Regarding `reserve_space`, there is also the behavior from the underlying `oa_hash_map` that doubles its size when you use 90% of the space:  
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/134da374975114ef8e05cf81d1d30eff645e310e/core/templates/oa_hash_map.h#L211-L214  
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/134da374975114ef8e05cf81d1d30eff645e310e/core/templates/oa_hash_map.h#L185-L187  

I was wondering why I was getting those weird values in my reported [issue](https://github.com/Zehir/godot-hexagon-tile-map-layer/issues/1#issuecomment-2700799873).

So, if you know that you will need exactly 100 points, you can't just call `reserve_space(100)`, because at the insertion of the 90th point, it will double its capacity, and you will end up with a capacity of 200.

And if you have 100 points to add, you should reserve at least for 112 points. With only 111, you will reach 90% and end up with a capacity of 222. That why multiply by 1.12 does the trick.

There are two cases:
1. If you `reserve_space(num_nodes)` before adding points, you will end up with `num_nodes * 2` capacity at the end.
2. If you don't reserve the space, your capacity will be a power of 2 (starting at 64). The complete hashmap will be resized multiple times when you reach 90%, which, as I understand, is something you want to avoid.

Here is a table with the limits when you don't reserve the space:

| Point count | Capacity |
|-------------|----------|
| 0           | 64       |
| 58          | 128      |
| 116         | 256      |
| 231         | 512      |
| 461         | 1024     |
| 922         | 2048     |

For example, with 460 points, you have a capacity of 512, but with 461 points, you have a capacity of 1024.
